newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

The rally of robusta futures in London ran out of steam although arabica futures in New York continued to soar. March ended $10 lower at $1,640 per tonne, while May gave up $7 to close at $1,660 per tonne. Apparently players became nervous as robusta coffee is in greater supply than arabicas and therefore there is greater danger of a set back. Another factor was that speculators wanted to take profits ahead of the weekend.

In New York arabica futures surged for the sixth straight session to above 180 cents/lb basis March. March added 8.20 cents/lb to close at 180.05 cents/lb, while May ended 5.80 cents/lb higher at 169.00 cents/lb. The rise was ascribed to speculative buying and traders covering short positions. Furthermore, first notice is looming just around the corner and open interest remains high with little likelihood of any coffee being moved to the board for certification and delivery as physical prices are still higher in spite of the recent advance in futures. This suggests that supplies remain very tight. However, in spite of tight supplies, the danger of a correction has become more acute after the recent sharp rises. But most traders have little doubt that supplies will remain tight throughout the year.

COSTA RICA - Costa Rica's 1996/97 (October/September) coffee crop is only half sold, leaving about 1 million 60-kg bags unsold, as a result, trade sources said. It was added that the country will be able to sell coffee at higher prices, allowing local farmers and exporters to receive higher payments than they had expected at the beginning of the crop. Total production in 1996/97 could be around 2.3 million bags of which roughly 2 million bags for export, down from 2.6 million bags produced the previous year.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 1.25 million 60-kg bags of coffee, ground and in beans, in January 1997, sharply up from the 589,340 bags shipped the same month the previous year, but down from the revised December 1996 figure of 1.52 million bags, the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters said. Exports receipts in January were $160.14 million compared with $75.20 million in the same month last year. Of the total shipped, 1.22 million bags were of arabica coffee, while robusta (conillon) accounted for just 21,600 bags.

ITALY - Italy imported 228,208 bags of coffee in August 1996, 7.6 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 3.707 million bags, 4 percent more than was imported the like period in 1995. Total imports in calendar 1995 dropped by 1.6 percent to 5.387 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Cameroon (278,900 vs 243,500 bags), Ivory Coast (294,800 vs 307,200 bags), Uganda (203,800 vs 182,800 bags), Zaire (335,700 vs 479,800 bags), Brazil (787,000 vs 978,000 bags), Colombia (255,500 vs 192,300 bags), India (300,400 vs 251,900 bags) and Vietnam (149,200 vs 61,500 bags). The country exported 524,100 bags of coffee in January/August 1996, 16 percent more than was in the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar 1995 rose by 5.2 percent to 738,900 bags.
